title: Choose Tavern's visual world
question: The roll assigned Swiss Grid Register. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Swiss Grid Register
options.lineage: International Typographic Style: Müller-Brockmann grid systems, objective information design
options.thesis: Knowledge as an objective register: one grotesk, a strict modular grid, flat color fields that code item type, and no ornament anywhere.
options.viewport: Flush-left headings in a wide bold grotesk, a column grid you can feel, the active section as a solid ultramarine field, items listed as a typeset register with owner and freshness columns.
options.risk: Strict restraint can feel cold; it needs the color fields and confident type scale to keep warmth and hierarchy.

options.label: Data Field
options.lineage: Ryoji Ikeda datamatics: black/white barcode fields, monospace numerics
options.thesis: The project as a dense data field; every access and change rendered as crisp numerics.
options.case: Fuses poorly overall: strictly black and white leaves no way to code item types or states, though it would suit the audit log.

options.label: Movement Score
options.lineage: Labanotation dance scores: a vertical staff read upward, shaded blocks
options.thesis: Onboarding as a score: each step a block whose length is its effort, read upward through time.
options.case: Fuses poorly: it could carry onboarding progress but has no vocabulary for a searchable knowledge list.

options.label: Full-bleed Feed
options.lineage: Vertical video feed surfaces: one item per viewport, action rail
options.thesis: One resource at a time, full screen, with the next one a flick away.
options.case: Fuses poorly: people scan and compare many resources at once, so a one-at-a-time view hides what they need.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: Modern B2B SaaS done straight: neutral grays, one blue accent, sidebar and tables at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar navigation, project header, filterable knowledge list.
